newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Backstrom sees inflation 1.5-2.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Backstrom sees inflation 1.5-2.0 pct.

text.p: The governor of Sweden's central bank, Urban Backstrom,said on Friday he saw the consumer price index rising but did not expect underlying inflation to increase.
Backstrom told reporters he saw underlying inflation at 1.5 to 2.0 percent.
"It is conceivable that CPI rises some but not underlying inflation," Backstrom said outside an European Union committee meeting.
Backstrom declined to comment on the surprise 0.4 percent fall in August consumer prices, which came against market expectations for prices to stay flat.
This brought inflation on an annualised basis down to 0.3 percent, its lowest since 1959.
Backstrom said this was "a positive surprise" but he did not want to say more until the central bank, the Riksbank, releases its inflation report on September 24.
He did say: "The market will recognise the monetary policy that will be carried out."
He said he saw underlying inflation staying around 1.5 to 2.0 percent. The government has set an inflation target of an annual 2.0 percent for the next two years.
Asked about Sweden's participation in Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), Backstrom reaffirmed earlier comments that the Riksbank is positive toward EMU links.
"It is reasonable that Sweden goes into the EMU," he said.
He said Sweden had a good chance to meet the convergence criteria needed for EMU participation as the low inflation level ought to lead to reduced fluctuations in the public finances.
